content: The International Diabetes Federation (IDF) is a global coalition comprising 200 diabetes associations from over 150 countries. Its primary mission is to improve the lives of individuals living with diabetes worldwide. For more than 50 years, the IDF has been at the forefront of global diabetes advocacy, striving to raise awareness about diabetes, promote appropriate care and prevention strategies, and support efforts to discover cures for various types of diabetes. The IDF is dedicated to advancing diabetes care, prevention, and cure on a global scale. It brings together key stakeholders from the international diabetes community, including individuals with diabetes and their families, healthcare professionals, diabetes organizations, and commercial partners whose goals align with the IDF’s mission. These stakeholders collaborate to establish shared objectives and coordinate activities to achieve these goals. The IDF is affiliated with the United Nations Department of Public Information and maintains official relations with the World Health Organization (WHO) and the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO). In December 2006, the IDF issued a press release highlighting the alarming prevalence of diabetes, which then affected 246 million people globally. Of these, 46% were aged between 40 and 59 years. Previous estimates had underestimated the scale of the problem, and even the most pessimistic predictions fell short of the current reality. The IDF projected that, without intervention, the number of people living with diabetes would rise to 380 million within 20 years. The IDF conducts numerous programs aimed at improving diabetes care and educating both the public and healthcare professionals about the disease. As of 2007, these programs included initiatives such as the IDF Task Force on Insulin, Test Strips, and Other Diabetes Supplies; the IDF Task Force on Clinical Practice Guidelines; the IDF Consultative Section on Diabetes Education (DECS); and the development of a worldwide definition of metabolic syndrome. Other programs addressed type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and the metabolic syndrome in Europe, as well as the definition and diagnosis of diabetes mellitus and intermediate hyperglycemia. The IDF also launched a Child Sponsorship Program to support children with diabetes. The IDF has published several key resources, including the Diabetes Atlas, Third Edition, the 19th World Diabetes Congress Abstract Book, and various educational modules. Other notable publications include Diabetes and Foot Care: Time to Act, the Global Guideline for Type 2 Diabetes, and the IDF Consensus Worldwide Definition of the Metabolic Syndrome. Additional works focus on topics such as diabetes and obesity, kidney disease, cost-effective approaches to diabetes care, and global strategies to raise awareness about diabetes. The IDF has also compiled and disseminated data under the Did You Know? initiative, which highlights the prevalence and impact of diabetes. These data reveal the urgent need for targeted efforts to address the diabetes epidemic. Key findings include the following: Each year, approximately 7 million new cases of diabetes are diagnosed. Every 10 seconds, one person develops diabetes, and another dies from diabetes-related complications. Diabetes is the fourth leading cause of death globally. Around 50% of individuals with diabetes are unaware of their condition, with this figure reaching as high as 80% in some countries. Type 2 diabetes can be prevented in up to 80% of cases through a healthy diet and increased physical activity, such as moderate exercise and walking. Diabetes is a leading cause of kidney failure, with 10–20% of individuals with diabetes dying from renal failure.
